scientific_question: Which LC-MS/MS entities show a drug-mixture-associated 72-hour response in microbial communities beyond both the no-drug community endpoint and the matched abiotic medium response?
primary_estimand: equal-weight mean across four communities of (microbial drug T72 - microbial no-drug T72), minus (BHI drug T72 - BHI no-drug T72)
sensitivity_estimand: historical (microbial T72-T0)-(BHI T72-T0), written separately and not interpreted as drug-specific because no-drug community growth is absent

prespecified_biological_truth.basis: published before this cross-project response analysis

exclusions.drug_mix5: not one of the four mixtures defined in the published Methods
exclusions.48_hour_groups: fast and medium-fast communities excluded from the primary common-time estimand because the matched abiotic endpoint is 72 hours

claim_boundary: MSV000095331 is a new experiment/project but shares the Dorrestein research ecosystem with the ChemProp sources; it is not independent-laboratory confirmation.
The primary endpoint interaction removes the deposited no-drug endpoint and abiotic response; it does not establish a single-drug causal effect inside a multi-drug mixture.
A mixture response cannot establish which co-administered drug caused a feature response.
Three paired response replicates provide only two degrees of freedom; normal-approximation p-values are prohibited and feature-wise significance is exploratory even with a t reference.
Library-supported means a stringent public-library match, not level-1 identification.
The paper's named drug products are validation targets and do not enter feature filtering or beta/SE estimation.
